title: Five smooth stones (1 Samuel 17)
hook: a shepherd refuses the king's armor and faces the giant with a sling

segments.voice: Yesterday, the harp, and Saul refreshed. Your line was music can heal.

Two armies on two hills, a valley between, and morning and evening a champion walks out: Goliath of Gath, in a helmet of brass and a coat of mail, with a spear like a weaver's beam. "I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together." Nobody goes. Saul and all Israel are dismayed, and greatly afraid. A shepherd boy arrives from Bethlehem with grain and loaves for his brothers, and cheeses for their captain. He asks who this Philistine is, "that he should defy the armies of the living God?" His eldest brother, Eliab, the one Samuel almost anointed, is furious. The question reaches the king.
screen: `A BOY WITH LOAVES FOR HIS BROTHERS.`

segments.voice: Saul says what anyone would: "Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth." David answers with his résumé, and it's all sheep. A lion took a lamb; he went after it. A bear too. "The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine." Saul does the kindest thing he knows. He dresses David in his own armor: helmet of brass, coat of mail, his sword. Saul stood higher than any of the people, and some readers point out he was the obvious one to face the giant. Instead he hands his gear to a boy. David tries to walk in it, and stops: "I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him." The armor isn't bad. It's Saul's, and David has never fought in it. He takes what he has tested: "he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag." His sling in his hand. The text never says why five. Mocked, David answers, "Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts." One stone sinks into the giant's forehead, and he falls on his face. Then, quietly: "there was no sword in the hand of David." Saul's sword was left behind with the borrowed armor.
screen: `THE LION, THE BEAR, AND THIS PHILISTINE.`
`NO SWORD IN THE HAND OF DAVID.`

segments.voice: Name one giant you're facing, a hard conversation, a fear, and notice whose armor you've been wearing for it. Then ask what's already in your bag, what you've tested, patience, humor, honesty, and choose one, the way David chose a stone. If you pray, bring the giant before God.
Sling. The shepherd's weapon that sent one of five smooth stones into the giant's forehead.
Your line: not in saul's armor. David went with what he had tested. Day seven hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Christians tell the story of David and Goliath to children and adults alike, and read David's words, I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, as trust in God rather than in weapons.

notes: Audit: "almost a joke" about the text changed to "a quiet, pointed line" (no humor at the text's expense).
Editor 2: practice opener 'Bring to mind' (used on days 712 and 714) varied; no factual changes needed.

'Saul stood higher than any of the people' rests on 1 Samuel 10:23 ('higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward'); the point that he was the obvious one to face Goliath is attributed to 'some readers'.

Editor: Goliath's challenge is now 'morning and evening' per 17:16 (was 'every morning'); the food is split as the text has it, grain and loaves for the brothers (17:17) and cheeses for the captain (17:18), in voice and screen.
(Superseded) The 'bread and cheese' combined 17:17 (parched corn and loaves for the brothers) and 17:18 (ten cheeses for the captain); confirm the summary is fair or simplify to 'food'.
Goliath's height (six cubits and a span in the Hebrew and KJV; four cubits in some Greek and Qumran texts) is deliberately not given.
'Saul's sword' follows 17:39 (David girded his sword upon his armor); 'left behind with the borrowed armor' follows 17:39–40 (he put them off) and 17:50.
The text gives no reason for five stones; later guesses (e.g. Goliath's kin in 2 Samuel 21) are left out.
Original: קֶלַע (KEH-la), sling; 17:40 has וְקַלְעוֹ. Confirm.
The final killing with Goliath's own sword (17:51) is left out to keep the day on the armor.
